def f(g):
    h,w=len(g),len(g[0])
    cnt={}
    for r in g:
        for v in r: cnt[v]=cnt.get(v,0)+1
    bg=max(cnt,key=cnt.get); mk=[v for v in cnt if v!=bg][0]
    res=[[g[r][c] for c in range(w)] for r in range(h)]
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if g[r][c]!=mk: continue
            row9=[cc for cc in range(w) if g[r][cc]==mk]
            col9=[rr for rr in range(h) if g[rr][c]==mk]
            if (any(cc<c for cc in row9) and any(cc>c for cc in row9)) or \
               (any(rr<r for rr in col9) and any(rr>r for rr in col9)):
                res[r][c]=2
    return res

import numpy as np, collections
# Hypothesis: fill bg cell if it's within distance <=K of a marker on some axis (toward grid edge or another marker?) 
# First inspect: for each bg cell, distances to nearest marker (up/down/left/right), and whether filled
def feats(g):
    g=np.array(g); h,w=g.shape
    cnt=collections.Counter(g.flatten().tolist()); bg=cnt.most_common(1)[0][0]
    nmk=[v for v in cnt if v!=bg and v!=2][0]
    res=[]
    for r in range(h):
        for c in range(w):
            if g[r,c]!=bg: continue
            us=[y-r for y in list(np.where(g[:,c]==nmk)[0]) if y<r]
            ds=[r-y for y in list(np.where(g[:,c]==nmk)[0]) if y>r]
            ls=[c-x for x in list(np.where(g[r]==nmk)[0]) if x<c]
